validation_note: Every case in this batch is supported by at least one official or public institutional source. Analogies are not automatic diagnoses for Olszówka/Gardeja.

cases.name: Dead Sea
cases.observed_pattern: Diversion of inflow for agriculture reduced the water reaching this terminal lake and contributed to major shoreline retreat and separation of the southern basin.
cases.management_lesson: In a terminal basin with no surface outlet, sustained upstream abstraction accumulates over time; management must account for the entire inflow budget rather than the lake alone.

provenance.title: Dead Sea
provenance.supports: Diversion of water flowing into the Dead Sea for agriculture and resulting dramatic retreat.

cases.name: Doñana wetlands
cases.observed_pattern: UNESCO has repeatedly reported poor quantitative condition and over-exploitation in groundwater bodies supporting the Doñana wetland system.
cases.management_lesson: Wetland decline can be driven by groundwater pressure even when surface channels remain visible; aquifer status, recharge and abstraction thresholds belong in the same monitoring system as surface-water extent.

provenance.title: Decision 47 COM 7B.31 — Doñana National Park
provenance.supports: Three groundwater bodies remain in poor quantitative condition due to ongoing over-exploitation; closure of illegal wells and sustainable extraction thresholds are part of the response.

cases.name: Greater Everglades
cases.observed_pattern: Canals, levees and water-control infrastructure altered natural sheetflow, hydrologic connectivity and the timing and distribution of freshwater through the wetland.
cases.management_lesson: Connectivity is a measurable hydrologic variable. Restoration should test flow paths, barriers, timing and distribution rather than treating wetland area alone as the health metric.

provenance.title: Geology and Hydrology of Everglades National Park
provenance.supports: Water levels and flow patterns are largely controlled by levees and canals originally built for flood control, drainage and supply.

provenance.title: Water Velocity Mapping of the L-67C Canal in support of the Decompartmentalization Physical Model
provenance.supports: Major barriers to natural flow and a field test of reconnection using culverts, levee removal and canal backfilling.

cases.name: Colorado River Delta
cases.observed_pattern: A 2014 binational environmental pulse released water into a formerly dry delta channel; monitoring showed both channel response and substantial infiltration to groundwater.
cases.management_lesson: Environmental releases should be instrumented as experiments: surface-water extent alone can miss large infiltration losses and aquifer recharge, so surface and groundwater responses must be measured together.

provenance.title: Geomorphic change in the Limitrophe reach of the Colorado River in response to the 2014 delta pulse flow
provenance.supports: Minute 319 enabled an environmental pulse into the dry channel; discharge declined downstream.

provenance.title: Groundwater response to the 2014 pulse flow in the Colorado River Delta
provenance.supports: Most pulse-flow water infiltrated and recharged the aquifer; groundwater pumping affected storage potential.

cases.name: Lake Tuz
cases.observed_pattern: After 2000 the saline lake became much more sensitive to drought, coinciding with excessive use of groundwater and surface-water resources feeding the lake, rerouted streams and dams.
cases.management_lesson: When drought sensitivity changes over time, test whether human withdrawals have reduced the basin's hydrologic buffer; compare climate anomalies with abstraction and feeder-stream continuity.

provenance.title: Disappearing Lake Tuz
provenance.supports: Drought combined with excessive groundwater and surface-water use, rerouting and damming of streams feeding the lake.

cases.name: Tulare Lake basin
cases.observed_pattern: Rivers that historically filled the basin were dammed and diverted; during exceptionally wet 2023 conditions, water returned and reoccupied parts of the former lakebed.
cases.management_lesson: Topographic depressions retain their flood function after land-use change. Historical lakebeds and flow paths should remain in flood-risk and storage planning even after decades of apparent dryness.

provenance.title: Return of Tulare Lake
provenance.supports: Historic feeder rivers were dammed/diverted; heavy precipitation and snowmelt refilled parts of the former basin in 2023.

cases.name: Lake Prespa
cases.observed_pattern: Long-term water-level decline is linked to climate pressure, irrigation use and continuous underground karst losses toward Lake Ohrid; temporary high rainfall in 2026 raised levels without proving full ecological recovery.
cases.management_lesson: A lake can lose water through subsurface outlets that are invisible in ordinary imagery. Temporary level recovery should not be confused with recovery of the long-term water balance or ecosystem.

provenance.title: When More Water Is Not Enough? Restoring Prespa’s Lifelines, Not Just Its Levels
provenance.supports: Reduced rainfall, higher temperatures, irrigation use and underground karst losses; 2026 rainfall increased levels but is not treated as full recovery.

provenance.title: Restoration of the Prespa Lake Ecosystem
provenance.supports: Eutrophication drivers and restoration actions involving agriculture, erosion, wastewater, wetland restoration and monitoring.

cases.name: Menindee Lakes / Lower Darling-Baaka
cases.observed_pattern: A shallow semi-arid lake system experiences large evaporation losses and variable inflow; current basin management explicitly protects environmental water and tests how it is shepherded through the connected river-lake system.
cases.management_lesson: In connected regulated systems, water accounting and protection rules can be as important as physical infrastructure; track whether environmental water actually survives the journey through the basin.

provenance.publisher: NSW Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
provenance.title: Northern to southern Basin environmental flow protection trial
provenance.supports: Environmental inflows are actively protected through Menindee Lakes and downstream toward the Murray Mouth.

provenance.title: Menindee Lakes project
provenance.supports: Shallow hot semi-arid lakes experience large annual evaporation losses and are operated as part of the Murray supply system.

cases.name: Lake Victoria — water quality
cases.observed_pattern: Water quality degradation is driven by pollution from settlements, industry and land use across a transboundary basin, with ecological and public-health consequences.
cases.management_lesson: A water-management system must measure quality as well as quantity. Basin-wide pollution sources and wetland buffer loss can degrade a lake even when surface area appears stable.

provenance.title: Reviving Lake Victoria: A Regional Approach to Inclusive Sanitation
provenance.supports: Pollution from inadequate sanitation, poor land practices and industrial waste is degrading water quality and fish stocks; coordinated regional management is required.

cases.name: Chao Lake
cases.observed_pattern: A large lake-basin rehabilitation program combines institutional reform, digital decision support, ecological compensation and low-carbon water-quality restoration measures.
cases.management_lesson: Large-scale water restoration benefits from a decision-support layer that combines monitoring, governance, incentives and physical ecological measures instead of relying on one engineering action.

provenance.title: Anhui Chao Lake Environmental Rehabilitation Project (Phase 2)
provenance.supports: Integrated lake-basin management, digital decision support, climate-resilient development, water-quality improvement and ecological restoration.
